title: Knowledge and Attitudes Towards Mental Disorders in Older Age
summary: Older adults with mental disorders are underprovided with adequate care. Although depression and dementia are among the most common mental disorders in older age, only a small proportion of affected individuals receive guideline-concordant treatment, often in the context of insufficient diagnostic assessment. The reasons for this are multifaceted and are assumed to lie on the side of healthcare providers, patients, as well as broader environmental factors. The aim of the present study is to examine knowledge and attitudes toward mental disorders in older age among psychology students and to investigate the influence of language (stigmatizing versus appreciative) on their attitudes.
conditions: Dementia in other diseases classified elsewhere

interventions.name: The present study is an anonymous online survey building on a previous study (Wuttke et al., 2023; doi: 10.1016/j.pmedr.2023.102384).
